Class TypeHierarchies

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.core.type.TypeHierarchies
public final class TypeHierarchies extends Object
Finds the TypeHierarchy records a compilation wrote.

A record is a generated class, registered as a META-INF/micronaut service of TypeHierarchy, whose name says which type it describes. A lookup reads the names of the service entries of the class loader, which the service index of a packaged application already holds, and loads the one record of the type asked for: no other record is loaded, and the class asked about is not read reflectively. Each lookup instantiates the record anew, which is a handful of Arguments; a caller that asks for a hierarchy repeatedly keeps it.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • invalidate

      public static void invalidate()
      Forgets the records found so far, for a class path that changed. A lookup that overlaps the call can still publish what it read before the change; a caller that reloads classes invalidates after the change is complete.

    • recordClassName

      @Internal public static String recordClassName(String typeName, String recordPackage)
      The name of the record of a type. A record written into the package of the type is named after the type, com.example.$Foo$TypeHierarchy for com.example.Foo. A record written into another package, as a record of a public class of a library or of the JDK is, goes into a sub-package of that package named after the package of the type, with $$ in front of its first segment: com.example.$$java.util.$ArrayList$TypeHierarchy. Every segment stays a Java identifier, so no character of a type name is escaped and the type name reads back without ambiguity; a source package whose segment starts with $$ is not expected.
      Parameters:
      typeName - The name of the type
      recordPackage - The package the record is written into
      Returns:
      The name of the record
